metadata.title: Sarah Guo — No Priors, Just Conviction

conclusion: Sarah Guo is long the AI wager and will not tap the brakes: a friend wants to, but is going 90 mph. Conviction's edge is staying close to ~250 frontier builders — not a backtest. She wants high-agency people plus risk capital so open-source and US industrial policy do not collapse into a two-lab monolith. Compute is the constraint: $750B-class spend empties individual ownership. Sunday Robotics (Tony Zhao, Chenxi; Stanford / Toyota / DeepMind / Tesla) is the physical-world print. She raised on execute-like-hell, not a polished deck. Abundant intelligence is not inevitable when supply chains are fragile.
background: First ILTB with Guo as Conviction founder (also known from No Priors). Patrick pushes on frenzy, the lab-vs-everyone-else wager, LP ranking, and how you invest when you cannot backtest. Topics: talent race, robotics, biology, open source, and what changes in the next year.
important_facts: Positioning: Guo answers 'I'm a long' on the AI wager. The fear is missing the opportunity versus repeating every boom-bust. Partner Mike maps ~250 entrepreneurs/researchers who actually show up and push the frontier; the firm's job is to know and support them, not just take first meetings. An LP survey of who fancy LPs most want to invest with had Conviction #1 or #2. She rejects a two-lab monolith: high-agency people plus the right risk capital can change open-source and industrial-policy outcomes.

Compute and product: major labs are so compute-intensive that a $750B spend plus thousands of people makes ownership feel thin. First-year hunt was technology-forward — workflows and professions that fit the models, which many LPs called nonsense versus customer-problem-first. Robotics example: she and partner Pranav met Tony Zhao and Chenxi at Sunday Robotics as Stanford PhDs after Toyota Research, DeepMind, and Tesla. Book also spans biology, defense, and law; she spends days-to-weeks grounding each domain. Open source is a policy and ecosystem question, not a slogan.

Firm-building: she raised by saying there are things she imagines about culture, then 'we'll go execute like hell and figure it out' — hard for LPs, which she values. Parents taught integrity, independence of thought, and family/team focus. She starts at conviction and works backwards (Mike climbs to it). Debates inside the firm and a biology opportunity close the hour. Abundant intelligence is not inevitable if compute stays scarce and supply chains stay fragile.

mental_model.name: No-Backtest Long × 250-Person Map × Compute Independence
mental_model.components: You cannot backtest this cycle; the mistake is hitting the brakes at 90 mph or repeating every bust. Map the ~250 people who actually push the frontier and stay close. Bet high-agency founders plus risk capital against a two-lab monolith. Treat $750B compute as the constraint that empties individual ownership. Hunt workflows the models already fit, not only customer-problem decks. Physical-world (Sunday Robotics) and biology are the non-obvious books. Raise on execute-like-hell, not a polished prior.
mental_model.application: Conviction is the private vehicle. NVDA remains the compute substrate of the $750B problem. Sunday Robotics is the humanoid/physical tell from this tape. Fade 'abundant intelligence is inevitable' if power, wafers, and policy stay tight. Do not wait for a backtest to size the AI book. Open-source industrial policy is a second-order bet, not a trading signal today.

key_insights.question: Brake or miss it?
key_insights.answer: A friend wants to brake and still goes 90 mph. Guo is a long. Missing it and repeating every bust are both live.

key_insights.question: What is the firm actually?
key_insights.answer: Proximity to the builders who show up, not a meeting machine. LPs already rank them #1 or #2.

key_insights.question: Why independence?
key_insights.answer: $750B spend plus thousands of heads. Fragile supply chains make compute independence a national and firm problem.

top_investment_implications.thesis: The 250-person map plus execute-like-hell raise is the product; LP demand is already #1/#2 — medium
Default substrate under the $750B compute constraint she names; not a new chip thesis — low
Named physical-world bet (Zhao/Chenxi, Stanford/Tesla/DeepMind path) — low

golden_quotes: I keep saying I want to press the brakes as hard as I can, but I'm not doing it.
We'll go execute like hell and figure it out.
